title: Lester's light tone versus Herschel's big sound
summary: They discuss Lester's tone, its influence on later players like Stan Getz, and how Clayton came to admire it.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well actually Lester did get much more attention from the public and critics than Herschel, didn't he?

Yes. But Herschel got quite a bit of attention from playing, from having such a big sound, big tone on the tenor because most tenor players didn't have that big tone. And that is why Lester had been fired out of Fletcher Henderson's band because he didn't have a big tone.
And they said, man we can't make it with this cat because....... But you see what happened eventually that light tone became like Stan Getz. And all those guys were disciples of Lester's.
It's strange though because to me, well I mean I don't know what you thought, but it seemed wrong the sound, you know, it didn't seem ......

At first I thought that, but I got so later that I used to admire Lester. But I thought the sound, I always admired his technique and his improvisations. He could do some things I just, were unbelievable. But I always thought when I first heard him, I hadn't heard anybody play tenor. You see, I had been hearing Herschel out on the West Coast. And to me Herschel, Lester sounded more like, kind of like an alto.
But the more I worked around with him, especially on the Jazz at the Philharmonic, I liked him very well.
